text:
Match List I (Temple/Monument) with List II (Dynasty/Builder):

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. Jagannatha Temple, Puri | I. Hoysalas |
| B. Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur | II. Vijayanagara Empire |
| C. Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu | III. Eastern Gangas |
| D. Vitthala Temple, Hampi | IV. Cholas (Rajaraja I) |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
a) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
b) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
c) A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
d) A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
sol:
**Correct Option: (a)**

**Justification:**
The correct matching is **A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II**.
- **A-III:** by the end of the 12th century the Eastern Gangas had emerged as one of the most stable powers of eastern India, and this dynasty initiated the construction of the Jagannatha temple at Puri (NCERT Class 7, Exploring Society Part 2, p. 107).
- **B-IV:** the Brihadeeshwara temple at Thanjavur was built by Rajaraja Chola I (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, p. 37), and DSERT calls the marvellous Brihadishvara temple his contribution (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, p. 114).
- **C-I:** the military general Ketamalla built the Hoysaleshwara temple at Halebidu, a work of the Hoysala period (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, p. 42).
- **D-II:** the Vijaya Vitthala temple of Hampi is a Vijayanagara monument (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, pp. 39–40).

**Option (a): Correct.** It gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
**Option (b): Incorrect.** It gets C-I and D-II right but exchanges the first two rows, giving the Puri temple to the Cholas (A-IV) and the Thanjavur temple to the Eastern Gangas (B-III).
**Option (c): Incorrect.** It gets A-III and B-IV right but exchanges the two Karnataka rows, giving the Hoysaleshwara temple to Vijayanagara (C-II) and the Vitthala temple to the Hoysalas (D-I).
**Option (d): Incorrect.** Only B-IV and D-II are right; it gives the Puri temple to the Hoysalas (A-I) and the Hoysaleshwara temple to the Eastern Gangas (C-III).
Hence the correct answer is option (a).

**Result:** Puri's Jagannatha temple was begun by the Eastern Gangas, Thanjavur's Brihadeeshwara is Rajaraja Chola I's work, the Hoysaleshwara is Hoysala and the Vitthala temple at Hampi is Vijayanagara.

**Salient Features: The temples and their builders**
Two of the four temples in this match stand outside Karnataka, and the textbooks give them a good deal of attention.
- **The Nandi at Thanjavur:** a statue of the bull Nandi is commonly installed in front of Shiva temples, and DSERT describes the single-stone Nandi at the Brihadishvara temple as the largest in south India (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, p. 112).
- **A thousand years:** in 2010 the Reserve Bank of India brought out a "1000 Years of Brihadishvara Temple" coin of ₹1,000 face value (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, p. 113).
- **The deity at Puri:** by the twelfth century the principal deity at Puri had been identified as Jagannatha, literally "the lord of the world", a form of Vishnu (NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch 6, p. 141).
- **The Eastern Ganga realm:** their inscriptions claim a kingdom extending "from the Ganga to the Godavari", and they had marriage ties with the Cholas while also clashing with them (NCERT Class 7, Exploring Society Part 2, p. 107).

**Exam Fact:** In his northern campaign, Rajendra Chola I defeated Mahipala I of Bengal (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77).

text:
Consider the following statements:

Statement I: The Yelahanka Nadaprabhu family was founded by Kempegowda I, who ruled independently of Vijayanagara.
Statement II: During the reign of Kempegowda II, Bengaluru began to grow as a great centre of weaving.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
a) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
b) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
c) Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
d) Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
sol:
**Correct Option: (d)**

**Justification:**
**Statement I: Incorrect.** Both parts are wrong. The founder of the Yelahanka Nadaprabhu family was **Ranabhaire Gowda**, not Kempegowda I, and he was a **feudatory of Vijayanagara** who paid tribute to its rulers (II PUC History, Ch 5.4, PDF p. 154). DSERT likewise describes the Yelahanka Nadaprabhus as paleyagars under Vijayanagara (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 7, PDF p. 107).
**Statement II: Correct.** Kempegowda II was the son of Kempegowda I, and during his reign Bengaluru began to grow as a great centre of weaving (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 7, PDF p. 108).
**Option (d): Correct.** Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct. Options (a) and (b) accept the false Statement I, and option (c) reverses the two verdicts.
Hence the correct answer is option (d).

**Result:** The family began with Ranabhaire Gowda as a feudatory of Vijayanagara; Bengaluru grew as a weaving centre under Kempegowda II.

**Salient Features: The Nadaprabhus of Yelahanka**
The family rose as local rulers near Bengaluru under Vijayanagara.
- **Origin:** the family originally belonged to Putturu near Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu and later settled at Avati near Bengaluru; its family deity was Goddess Kempamma (II PUC History, Ch 5.4, PDF p. 154).
- **Kempegowda I's lakes:** Kempambudhi, Dharmambudhi, Halasuru and Sampangi (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 7, PDF p. 107).
- **Kempegowda I as ruler:** he built rest houses and agraharas, ruled as Dharmaprabhu and had the title "Praja Vatsala" (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 7, PDF p. 108).
- **Kempegowda II:** like his father, he became known for developing new villages and building temples and lakes (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 7, PDF p. 108).

**Exam Fact:** Magadi was an important trade centre in the time of the Yelahanka Nadaprabhus (II PUC History, Ch 5.4, PDF p. 154).

text:
The four-ashrama system of Brahmacharya, Gruhastha, Vaanaprastha and Sanyasa began in the
a) Rigvedic period
b) post-Vedic (Later Vedic) period
c) Mauryan period
d) Harappan period
sol:
**Correct Option: (b)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** DSERT calls the period of the Rigveda the "Pre-Vedic period" and the period of the other Vedas the "Post-Vedic period", and it places the start of the four ashramas in the latter (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF pp. 93, 95).
**Option (b): Correct.** The four-ashrama system (Chathurashrama) of Brahmacharya, Gruhastha, Vaanaprastha and Sanyasa started during the **post-Vedic period** (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 95).
**Option (c): Incorrect.** The system had already begun in the post-Vedic period, well before the Mauryas (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 95).
**Option (d): Incorrect.** The four ashramas belong to Vedic society as described in the Vedic texts. DSERT places their start in the post-Vedic period, not in the Harappan civilisation (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 95).
Hence the correct answer is option (b).

**Result:** The four ashramas began in the post-Vedic (Later Vedic) period.

**Salient Features: Pre-Vedic and post-Vedic society**
DSERT traces how society changed between the two Vedic periods.
- **Texts of the later period:** the Later Vedic period is that of the Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 35).
- **Women in the pre-Vedic period:** women studied the Vedas and widow remarriage was in practice; Ghosha, Apala, Lopamudra, Indrani and Vishwavara were scholars of the Vedic period (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 93).
- **Women in the post-Vedic period:** the position of women was lowered, and they were deprived of education (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 95).
- **Family:** in the pre-Vedic period the family was the basic unit, the father was its head and the joint family system was in practice (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 93).

**Exam Fact:** The gotra system also started during the post-Vedic period (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 95).

text:
With reference to the Buddhist councils and the spread of Buddhism, which of the following statements are correct?
1. The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha under the patronage of Ajatashatru.
2. The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra and was convened by Ashoka.
3. Kanishka sent Buddhist missionaries to Central Asia and China.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
a) 1 and 2 only
b) 2 and 3 only
c) 1 and 3 only
d) 1, 2 and 3
sol:
**Correct Option: (d)**

**Justification:**
**Statement 1: Correct.** The First Buddhist Council was held at **Rajgriha** under the patronage of **Ajatashatru** (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 16, PDF p. 7; II PUC History, Ch 4.2, PDF p. 49).
**Statement 2: Correct.** The Third Buddhist Council was held at **Pataliputra** (II PUC History, Ch 4.2, PDF p. 49), and it was convened by **Ashoka** (Tamil Nadu History textbook, p. 52; DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 16, PDF p. 7).
**Statement 3: Correct.** Like Ashoka, Kanishka sent missionaries to **Central Asia and China** to spread Buddhism (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 16, PDF p. 7).
All three statements are correct, which is option (d). Option (a) omits the true 3, option (b) omits the true 1 and option (c) omits the true 2.
Hence the correct answer is option (d).

**Result:** Rajgriha under Ajatashatru, Pataliputra under Ashoka, and Kanishka's missions to Central Asia and China are all correct.

**Salient Features: The four Buddhist councils**
The councils were called to settle the teachings and the differences among monks.
- **First Council:** it compiled the sayings of the Buddha (II PUC History, Ch 4.2, PDF p. 49).
- **Second Council:** it was held at Vaishali (II PUC History, Ch 4.2, PDF p. 49), and DSERT names Kalasoka as its patron (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 16, PDF p. 7).
- **Fourth Council:** it was held at Kundalavana in Kashmir (II PUC History, Ch 4.2, PDF p. 49), in the reign of Kanishka (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 16, PDF p. 7).

**Exam Fact:** At the Third Buddhist Council, the Kathavatthu was added as the last section of the Abhidhamma Pitaka (Tamil Nadu History textbook, p. 52).

text:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. Sekkilar | I. Jeevaka Chintamani |
| B. Thirukkadeva | II. Periya Purana |
| C. Rajendra Chola I | III. Built the new capital, Gangaikonda-cholapuram |
| D. Rajendra Chola III | IV. Ruler under whom the Chola empire weakened and the Pandyas overpowered it |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
a) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
b) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
c) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
d) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
sol:
**Correct Option: (c)**

**Justification:**
The correct pairing is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.
- **Sekkilar:** he composed the Periya Purana (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, PDF p. 41). Sekkilar–II.
- **Thirukkadeva:** he wrote the Jeevaka Chintamani (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, PDF p. 41). Thirukkadeva–I.
- **Rajendra Chola I:** after his northern campaign up to the Ganga he took the title "Gangaikonda Chola" and built a new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77; DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 6, PDF p. 132). Rajendra Chola I–III.
- **Rajendra Chola III:** the Chola empire weakened in his time, and the Pandyas could overpower it easily (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, PDF p. 39). Rajendra Chola III–IV.

**Option (a): Incorrect.** It swaps Sekkilar and Thirukkadeva (A-I, B-II).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** It swaps the two Rajendras (C-IV, D-III).
**Option (c): Correct.** It gives all four pairs correctly.
**Option (d): Incorrect.** It swaps Sekkilar and Rajendra Chola I (A-III, C-II).
Hence the correct answer is option (c).

**Result:** Sekkilar wrote the Periya Purana and Thirukkadeva the Jeevaka Chintamani; Rajendra I built Gangaikonda Cholapuram, and the empire weakened under Rajendra III.

**Salient Features: Rajendra Chola I and Chola culture**
Rajendra I's titles and works recall his campaigns and his patronage of learning.
- **Titles:** Rajendra Chola I had titles such as "Pandita Chola", "Gangaikonda Chola" and "Kedarakonda Deva" (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77).
- **Cholagangam:** near the new capital he built a huge irrigation lake named Cholagangam (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 6, PDF p. 132; II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77).
- **Vengi alliance:** Rajendra Chola I placed Rajaraja Narendra on the throne of Vengi and gave him his daughter Ammangadevi in marriage (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77).
- **Tamil literature:** besides the Periya Purana and the Jeevaka Chintamani, the Ramayana of Kamba is a noteworthy work of the Chola period (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, PDF p. 41).

**Exam Fact:** Rajendra Chola I sent his ambassadors to China in 1033 CE (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77).

text:
Arrange the following Kannada poets and saints in chronological order:
1. Basaveshwara
2. Kanakadasa
3. Pampa
4. Ranna

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
a) 1-3-4-2
b) 3-4-1-2
c) 3-1-4-2
d) 3-4-2-1
sol:
**Correct Option: (b)**

**Justification:**
The correct sequence is 3-4-1-2.
- **Pampa (3):** the Adikavi of Kannada was in the court of Arikesari II, a feudatory of the Rashtrakutas (II PUC History, Ch 4.8, PDF p. 99).
- **Ranna (4):** he was patronised by Satyashraya of the Chalukyas of Kalyana (II PUC History, Ch 4.9, PDF p. 104), the dynasty that rose when Tailapa II overthrew the Rashtrakutas (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 20, PDF p. 35).
- **Basaveshwara (1):** he lived from 1132 to 1168 CE (II PUC History, Ch 6, PDF p. 168).
- **Kanakadasa (2):** he lived from 1508 to 1606 CE (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 132).

**Option (a): Incorrect.** It puts Basaveshwara, a 12th-century figure, before the Rashtrakuta-period Pampa.
**Option (b): Correct.** It gives the order Pampa, Ranna, Basaveshwara, Kanakadasa.
**Option (c): Incorrect.** It puts Basaveshwara before Ranna, although Ranna belongs to the earlier Kalyana Chalukya court.
**Option (d): Incorrect.** It puts Kanakadasa (born 1508) before Basaveshwara (1132–1168).
Hence the correct answer is option (b).

**Result:** Pampa (Rashtrakuta period), then Ranna (Chalukyas of Kalyana), then Basaveshwara (1132–1168), then Kanakadasa (1508–1606).

**Salient Features: Basaveshwara and the vachana movement**
Basaveshwara's teaching joined devotion to social reform.
- **Parents:** his parents were Madarasa and Madalambike (II PUC History, Ch 6, PDF p. 168).
- **Kayakave Kailasa:** he held that work is a path to salvation and another form of devotion, and he upheld the dignity of labour (II PUC History, Ch 6, PDF p. 170).
- **Ashtavarana:** Lingayats follow eight principles taught at the time of deeksha, beginning with obedience to the Guru, worship of the Linga, reverence for the Jangama and smearing ashes on the forehead (II PUC History, Ch 6, PDF pp. 169–170).
- **Vachanakaras:** Jedara Dasimayya, Allamaprabhu, Chenna Basavanna and Akka Mahadevi were among the vachanakaras, who came from all castes and classes (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 16, PDF p. 87).

**Exam Fact:** Basaveshwara taught that a person should not hoard but practise Dasoha, the distribution of individual gains to society (II PUC History, Ch 6, PDF p. 170).

text:
Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
a) Mahendravarma – Mattavilasa Prahasana
b) Amarasimha – Amarakosha
c) Bharavi – a poet of the Gupta court of Chandragupta II
d) Durvineeta – a commentary on the fifteenth sarga of the Kiratarjuniya
sol:
**Correct Option: (c)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** The pair is correctly matched, so it is not the answer. The Pallava king Mahendravarma himself wrote the social drama "Matta Vilasa Prahasana" (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 19, PDF p. 28).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** The pair is correctly matched. Amarasimha, one of the Navaratnas of Chandragupta II's court, wrote the Amarakosha (II PUC History, Ch 4.5, PDF p. 72).
**Option (c): Correct.** This pair is NOT correctly matched, so it is the answer. Bharavi, author of the Kiratarjuniya, was a poet of the **Pallava court** (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 19, PDF p. 28). He is not among the Navaratnas of Chandragupta II's court listed in II PUC History (Ch 4.5, PDF p. 72).
**Option (d): Incorrect.** The pair is correctly matched. The Ganga king Durvineeta wrote a commentary (Bhashya) on the 15th sarga of Bharavi's Kiratarjuniya (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 6, PDF p. 113).
Hence the correct answer is option (c).

**Result:** Mahendravarma, Amarasimha and Durvineeta are correctly matched; Bharavi was a Pallava court poet, not a poet of Chandragupta II's court.

**Salient Features: Royal authors and court scholars**
Kings in this period were often scholars themselves as well as patrons.
- **Mahendravarma:** besides the Matta Vilasa Prahasana, he wrote the book Bhagavadajjukam; as he followed Jainism, there were many Jains in his kingdom (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 19, PDF p. 28).
- **Pallava Kanchi:** the Pallavas encouraged both Sanskrit and Tamil, and Kanchi was the centre of Sanskrit literature (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 19, PDF p. 28).
- **Durvineeta:** a scholar of Sanskrit and Kannada, he became heir to the Punnata royal family through his mother Jeshtadevi (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 6, PDF p. 113).
- **Navaratnas:** among the scholars at Chandragupta II's court, Varahamihira wrote the Brihatsamhita and Dhanvantari the Ayurveda Nighantu (II PUC History, Ch 4.5, PDF p. 72).

**Exam Fact:** Dharmapala, the great scholar of Nalanda University, was born in Kanchi (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 19, PDF p. 28).

text:
Correctly match the Kannada poets of the Vijayanagara period in List I with their works in List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. Kumaravyasa | I. Karnataka Bharata Kathamanjari (Gadugina Bharata) |
| B. Chamarasa | II. Prabhulingaleele |
| C. Ratnakaravarni | III. Bharateshavaibhava |
| D. Kanakadasa | IV. Ramadhanya Charite |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
a) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
b) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
c) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
d) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
sol:
**Correct Option: (d)**

**Justification:**
The correct matching is **A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV**.
- **A-I:** Kumaravyasa wrote the 'Karnata Bharata Katha Manjari' (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 14, p. 54), popularly known as the 'Gadugina Bharata' (II PUC History, Ch 5.4, PDF p. 150).
- **B-II:** Chamarasa's 'Prabhulingaleele' is the biography of Allamaprabhu (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 14, p. 54).
- **C-III:** Ratnakaravarni's 'Bharatesha Vaibhava' is a work written in an attractive style (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 14, p. 54).
- **D-IV:** Kanakadasa's important works are 'Mohanatarangini', 'Nalacharitre', 'Haribhaktisara' and 'Ramadhanyacharitre' (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, p. 38).

**Option (a): Incorrect.** It gets A-I and B-II right but exchanges the last two works, giving the Ramadhanya Charite to Ratnakaravarni (C-IV) and the Bharateshavaibhava to Kanakadasa (D-III).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** It gets C-III and D-IV right but exchanges the first two, giving the Prabhulingaleele to Kumaravyasa (A-II) and the Kannada Bharata to Chamarasa (B-I).
**Option (c): Incorrect.** It gets A-I and D-IV right but exchanges the middle two, giving the Bharateshavaibhava to Chamarasa (B-III) and the Prabhulingaleele to Ratnakaravarni (C-II).
**Option (d): Correct.** It gives A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.
Hence the correct answer is option (d).

**Result:** Kumaravyasa wrote the Kannada Bharata, Chamarasa the life of Allamaprabhu, Ratnakaravarni the Bharateshavaibhava and Kanakadasa the Ramadhanya Charite.

**Salient Features: Kannada literature in the Vijayanagara age**
Sanskrit, Kannada and Telugu literature all flourished during the Vijayanagara period (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 14, p. 54).
- **Kumaravyasa's name:** DSERT gives his personal name as Naranappa and calls him a poet of strong sentiments (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 14, p. 54).
- **The poets of the age:** the Gazetteer names Kumaravyasa, Chamarasa, Ratnakaravarni, Purandaradasa and Kanakadasa as the most notable Kannada poets of the time, and notes that almost all of them wrote on themes of their own religion (Karnataka Gazetteer 1982, Part 1, p. 298).
- **Virashaiva works:** the 'Shunyasampadane', a collection of the vachanas of Basavanna and his fellow sharanas, belongs to this period, and Lakkanna Dandesha wrote the 'Shivatatvachintamani' (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, p. 38).
- **The Dasas:** Purandaradasa, Kanakadasa, Shripadaraya and Vyasaraya enriched dasa sahitya (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, p. 38), and DSERT calls Purandaradasa the 'Father of Carnatic Music' (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 14, p. 54).

**Exam Fact:** Bheemakavi translated Palkurike Somanatha's Telugu 'Basavapurana' into Kannada (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, p. 37).

text:
After occupying the Javali region on the Konkan side, Shivaji built the new fort of
a) Sinhagad
b) Rajgad
c) Shivneri
d) Pratapgad
sol:
**Correct Option: (d)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** Sinhagad (Simhagad) was one of the forts Shivaji captured from the Adil Shah of Bijapur, not the new fort he built after occupying Javali (II PUC History, Ch 5.3, PDF p. 136).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** Rajgad is listed among Shivaji's important forts (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 17, PDF p. 16), but the new fort built after the occupation of Javali was Pratapgad.
**Option (c): Incorrect.** Shivneri in Pune district was Shivaji's birthplace (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 17, PDF p. 15).
**Option (d): Correct.** Shivaji turned his attention to the Konkan coast, occupied the region of Javali and built there the new fort of **Pratapgad** (II PUC History, Ch 5.3, PDF p. 136; DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 17, PDF p. 15).
Hence the correct answer is option (d).

**Result:** After taking Javali on the Konkan side, Shivaji built the new fort of Pratapgad.

**Salient Features: Shivaji's forts and army**
Forts were a major source of Shivaji's strength, and he organised them carefully.
- **Hawaldar:** the Hawaldar was the supervisor of a fort (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 17, PDF p. 16).
- **Against treachery:** three men of equal rank were placed in charge of each fort (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 180).
- **The army:** it had infantry, cavalry, elephant and cannon units, and the soldiers were specially trained in guerrilla warfare (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 17, PDF p. 16).
- **Silahdars:** besides the regular army there were silahdars, loose auxiliaries whose numbers varied from year to year according to need (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 180).

**Exam Fact:** Dadoji Kondadeo was Shivaji's guru, who trained him in armed warfare and the scriptures (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 17, PDF p. 15).

text:
The chaityagriha at Karle, of the Shatavahana period, was built by Bhootapala, who was a
a) Shatavahana king
b) general of Ashoka
c) Buddhist monk of Amaravati
d) merchant of Banavasi
sol:
**Correct Option: (d)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** Bhootapala was not a ruler. DSERT names him as a merchant of Banavasi (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** The chaityagriha belongs to the Shatavahana period, and its builder is named as a merchant, not an officer of Ashoka (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).
**Option (c): Incorrect.** He is named as a merchant of Banavasi, not as a monk of Amaravati (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).
**Option (d): Correct.** In the period of the Shatavahanas, a chaityagriha was built at Karle by the **Banavasi merchant Bhootapala** (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).
Hence the correct answer is option (d).

**Result:** The Karle chaityagriha was built by Bhootapala, a merchant of Banavasi.

**Salient Features: Life under the Shatavahanas**
DSERT describes the Shatavahanas as the first to establish a dynasty in the Deccan, in the land between the Godavari and the Krishna (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 16).
- **Administration:** the kingdom was divided into provinces called Janapadas under appointed officers, while cities and villages were looked after by self-governing institutions (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).
- **Occupations and trade:** farmers, merchants, goldsmiths, weavers and others formed occupational associations, which later grew into commercial and trade organisations; Nasik, Kalyan and Broach were among the trade centres (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).
- **Religion:** the Shatavahanas followed the Vedic tradition but also encouraged Buddhism and Jainism (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).
- **Women:** DSERT notes that women held high offices and had status in society (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 18, PDF p. 17).

**Exam Fact:** Many Satavahana coins depicted ships, which suggests that maritime trade was an important part of economic life (NCERT Class 7 Exploring Society Part 1, Ch 6, PDF p. 9).

text:
According to Ashoka's Major Rock Edict 3, which of the following groups of officials were instructed to go on tours every five years to instruct the people in dhamma?
a) Pativedakas
b) Yuktas, Rajjukas and Pradesikas
c) Amatyas
d) Dhamma Mahamatras
sol:
**Correct Option: (b)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** Ashoka arranged for pativedakas to report to him about the affairs of the people at all times and anywhere, whether he was eating, in the inner apartment or in the garden; epigraphists translate the term as "reporter" (NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part I, Ch 2, p. 47). They carried reports to the king; they are not the officials Edict 3 sends on tour.
**Option (b): Correct.** In Major Rock Edict 3, Ashoka instructed the yuktas (subordinate officials), rajjukas (rural administrators) and pradesikas (heads of the districts) to go on tours every five years to instruct people in dhamma (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 68).
**Option (c): Incorrect.** The amatyas were secretaries: three amatyas sat with three judges in the dharmasthiya courts and in the kantakasodhana courts (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 68). They are not the officials Edict 3 names.
**Option (d): Incorrect.** The dhamma mahamattas were special officers appointed to spread the message of dhamma (NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part I, Ch 2, p. 34). They form a separate post; the five-yearly tour of Edict 3 is laid on the yuktas, rajjukas and pradesikas.
Hence the correct answer is option (b).

**Result:** Edict 3 sends the yuktas, rajjukas and pradesikas on five-yearly tours to teach dhamma; the pativedakas reported to the king and the dhamma mahamattas were a separate post.

**Salient Features: Ashoka's officials and his dharmic state**
Ashoka's rule offers a model of a righteous king and a just state (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 68).
- **The king as parent:** his injunctions to officers and city magistrates stressed that all the people were his children and that he wished for them what he wished for his own children, welfare and happiness in this world and the next (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 68).
- **Impartial officials:** officers were to be impartial and to see that men were not imprisoned or tortured without good reason (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 68).
- **The rajukas:** Ashoka appointed a class of officers called rajukas, who had authority both to reward and to punish people where necessary (R.S. Sharma, *Ancient India*, p. 90).
- **The kantakasodhana courts:** the name means "removal of thorns"; these courts dealt with anti-social elements and crimes, worked rather like a modern police and relied on a network of spies (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 68).

**Exam Fact:** In Kalinga Rock Edict 1, Ashoka added that he would send an officer every five years to check whether his instructions were being carried out (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 68).

text:
Identify the correct statements about Purandaradasa from those given below:
1. His original name was Srinivasa Nayaka.
2. Vyasaraya gave him deeksha and called him "Purandara".
3. He composed his keertanas under the pen name "Purandara Vittala".
4. The Daasakoota was formed under his leadership.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
a) 1 and 3 only
b) 2 and 4 only
c) 1, 2 and 3 only
d) 1, 2, 3 and 4
sol:
**Correct Option: (c)**

**Justification:**
**Statement 1: Correct.** Purandaradasa was born in Purandaragada, and his original name was **Srinivasa Nayaka** (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 131).
**Statement 2: Correct.** Vyasaraya gave him deeksha and called him "Purandara"; he later became Purandaradasa (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 132).
**Statement 3: Correct.** He wrote his keertanas under the pen name **"Purandara Vittala"** (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 132).
**Statement 4: Incorrect.** The Daasakoota was formed under the leadership of **Shri Vyasaraya**, not Purandaradasa (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 74).
Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, which is option (c). Option (a) omits the true 2, option (b) omits the true 1 and 3 and includes the false 4, and option (d) includes the false 4.
Hence the correct answer is option (c).

**Result:** Srinivasa Nayaka, named "Purandara" by Vyasaraya, wrote as "Purandara Vittala"; the Daasakoota was led by Vyasaraya.

**Salient Features: Purandaradasa and the Dasa tradition**
The Dasas spread devotion through keertanas sung in Kannada.
- **Early life:** his parents were Varadappa Nayaka and Leelavathi; once a miser, he later gave away his wealth to the needy and spent the rest of his life in the thought of God (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 132).
- **Title:** he is known as "Karnataka Sangeetha Pithamaha" (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 132).
- **Kanakadasa:** another disciple of Vyasaraya, he composed keertanas under the pen name "Adikeshava" (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 133).
- **Land of Daasa Sahitya:** Raichur district of Kalaburagi division is called the land of Daasa Sahitya; keertanas were written by Kanakadasa, Purandaradasa and Raghavendratheertha (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 74).

**Exam Fact:** Vyasaraya praised his disciple with the words "Purandara Dasa is the Ultimate as a Dasa" (DSERT Class 7 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 8, PDF p. 132).

text:
With reference to Harappan towns, which of the following statements are correct?
1. Fire places have been found at Kalibangan and Lothal.
2. Harappan houses had windows facing the street.
3. Town drains were covered with stone slabs that had holes for regular maintenance.
a) 1 and 2 only
b) 1 and 3 only
c) 2 and 3 only
d) 1, 2 and 3
sol:
**Correct Option: (b)**

**Justification:**
**Statement 1: Correct.** Fire places are found in the towns of **Kalibangan and Lothal** (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 31).
**Statement 2: Incorrect.** The doors of Harappan houses faced the street, but **none of the windows were street-facing** (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 32).
**Statement 3: Correct.** Town drains were built of bricks and covered with stone slabs, and the cover slabs had **holes to enable regular maintenance** (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 32).
Statements 1 and 3 are correct, which is option (b). Options (a), (c) and (d) all include the false 2; option (a) also omits the true 3, and option (c) omits the true 1.
Hence the correct answer is option (b).

**Result:** Kalibangan and Lothal had fire places and the drain slabs had holes for maintenance; house windows did not face the street.

**Salient Features: Harappan houses, granaries and art**
Harappan towns were planned and built systematically.
- **Houses:** they were built of bricks with strong walls, generally of one or two storeys with rooms around an inner core; houses had baths, some with wells for water (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 32).
- **Drain upkeep:** DSERT notes that separate officers are understood to have been appointed to maintain the drains (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 32).
- **Granaries:** well-arranged granaries can be seen at Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro and Lothal (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 3, PDF p. 31); at Harappa a series of brick platforms formed the base for two rows of six granaries each (II PUC History, Ch 3, PDF p. 32).
- **Art:** the bronze idol of a dancing girl, a statue of a bearded man and figures of Pashupati show the Harappans' artistic skill (II PUC History, Ch 3, PDF p. 35).

**Exam Fact:** According to II PUC History, the largest building at Mohenjodaro is a granary 45.71 m long and 15.23 m wide (II PUC History, Ch 3, PDF p. 32).

text:
Which one of the following statements about the Cholas is NOT correct?
a) After the Pallavas, the Cholas held parts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra and Karnataka from the 9th to the 13th century.
b) The Chola kingdom was divided into mandalam, kottam, nadu and kurram.
c) Rajendra Chola's navy defeated the Srivijaya forces and annexed their empire as a Chola province.
d) The Cholas undertook large public works such as roads, tanks, wells, irrigation canals and artificial lakes.
sol:
**Correct Option: (c)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** The statement is correct, so it is not the answer. After the Pallavas, the Cholas secured a firm hold on many areas of Tamil Nadu, Andhra and Karnataka and ruled from the 9th to the 13th century (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, PDF p. 39).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** The statement is correct. DSERT lists the divisions as mandalam, kotwangi (kottam), nadu, kurram (a community of villages) and tara-kurram (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, PDF p. 40).
**Option (c): Correct.** The statement is NOT correct, so it is the answer. Rajendra's navy defeated the Shrivijaya forces and captured their capital, but **he did not try to occupy the defeated empire**; it was a punitive expedition (NCERT Class 7 Exploring Society Part 2, Ch 4, PDF p. 16).
**Option (d): Incorrect.** The statement is correct. The Cholas engaged in large public works, such as roads, tanks, wells and canals for irrigation, and artificial lakes (NCERT Class 7 Exploring Society Part 2, Ch 4, PDF p. 16).
Hence the correct answer is option (c).

**Result:** Rajendra's navy defeated Shrivijaya and took its capital, but the empire was not annexed; the other three statements are correct.

**Salient Features: The Cholas at sea and in the village**
The Cholas combined sea power abroad with strong village institutions at home.
- **Why Shrivijaya:** one of the sea routes to China passed through the Strait of Malacca, which the Shrivijaya king controlled, and this created competition with the Cholas (NCERT Class 7 Exploring Society Part 2, Ch 4, PDF p. 15).
- **Merchant guilds:** the expedition was conducted with the support of many Indian merchant guilds (NCERT Class 7 Exploring Society Part 2, Ch 4, PDF p. 16).
- **Kingship:** the Chola king was not absolute; the crown prince succeeded to the throne, and a council of ministers assisted the king (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77).
- **The king's circle:** the intimate group of the king was called the "Udanakootam" (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 77).

**Exam Fact:** Rajaraja Chola I permitted Srimara Vijayottungavarman, the Shailendra (Srivijaya) king, to build the Choodamani Buddhist vihara at Nagapattinam (II PUC History, Ch 4.6, PDF p. 76).

text:
Hoysala temples like those at Belur and Halebidu are famous for intricate carving mainly because they were built using which stone, which is soft when quarried and hardens on exposure to air?
a) Sandstone
b) Granite
c) Chloritic schist (soapstone)
d) Marble
sol:
**Correct Option: (c)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** In Kamath's account sandstone marks an earlier phase: the transitional temples of the Chalukyas of Kalyana at Konnur, Sudi, Savadi and Kukanur were built of coarse sandstone, but their later temples, like those of the Hoysalas, were built of chloritic schist or close-grained slate stone (Kamath, *A Concise History of Karnataka*, p. 124).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** The held accounts of Hoysala building name chloritic schist, not granite, as the material of the temples (Kamath, p. 142).
**Option (c): Correct.** The Hoysala temples were constructed in chloritic schist or slate stone, and their sculptures are highly ornate and finely finished (Kamath, p. 142). DSERT records that the Hoysalas carved their innumerable sculptures in soapstone (DSERT Class 8 Social Science Part 2, 2026-27, Ch 21, p. 41).
**Option (d): Incorrect.** Marble is not the material the sources give for the Hoysala temples; Kamath names chloritic schist (Kamath, p. 142).
Hence the correct answer is option (c).

**Result:** The Hoysala temples were built and carved in chloritic schist (soapstone), whereas the transitional Kalyana Chalukya temples at places like Konnur and Sudi used coarse sandstone.

**Salient Features: The Hoysala temple style**
Kamath treats Hoysala architecture as an offshoot of the Chalukyan style with enough independent features to count as a school of its own (Kamath, p. 140).
- **The plan:** the main temple has a garbhagriha, a shukanasi and a navaranga, and at times a mukhamantapa (Kamath, p. 140).
- **The outer walls:** the walls of the hall carry a procession of elephants at the bottom, a border of horsemen above it and a band of foliage, with a frieze of scenes from the epics above (Kamath, p. 141).
- **Doorways and screens:** the temple has a highly engraved doorway decorated with the makaratorana, and pierced windows or stone screens cover the upper parts of the navaranga (Kamath, pp. 141–142).
- **Number:** there are almost one hundred temples of this style, many in a bad state of preservation; temples at Basaralu, Tarikere, Arasikere and Mosalehalli are among those named (Kamath, p. 142).

**Exam Fact:** Kamath notes that the temple at Somanathapura has been regarded as illustrating the Hoysala style in its maturity (Kamath, *A Concise History of Karnataka*, p. 142).

text:
Madhura Vijayam, which describes Kampanna's invasion of the south, was written by
a) Lakkanna Dandesha
b) Gangadevi
c) Chamarasa
d) Kumaravyasa
sol:
**Correct Option: (b)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Incorrect.** Lakkanna Dandesha's work is the "Shivatatvachintamani" (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 51).
**Option (b): Correct.** Kampannaraya's wife **Gangadevi** wrote "Maduravijayam", which deals with Kampanna's invasion and describes places of pilgrimage (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 51).
**Option (c): Incorrect.** Chamarasa's work is the "Prabhulingaleele" (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 50).
**Option (d): Incorrect.** Kumaravyasa's work is the "Gaduginabharata" (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 50).
Hence the correct answer is option (b).

**Result:** Madhura Vijayam, on Kampanna's southern invasion, was written by his wife Gangadevi.

**Salient Features: Literature of the Vijayanagara period**
Works were written in Kannada, Sanskrit, Telugu and Tamil in this period (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 50).
- **Vidyaranya:** he wrote the "Shankaravijaya" and the "Sarvadarshana Samgraha" in Sanskrit (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 51).
- **Bheemakavi:** he translated Palkurike Somanatha's Telugu "Basavapurana" into Kannada (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF pp. 50–51).
- **Shunyasampadane:** a collection of the vachanas of Basavanna and his contemporary Sharanas (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 51).
- **Practical subjects:** Kannada books on human medicine, veterinary science, poetics, astrology and cookery also appeared (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 51).

**Exam Fact:** Sayanacharya, the brother of Vidyaranya, wrote commentaries on the Vedas called "Vedarthaprakasha" (DSERT Class 9 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, Ch 4, PDF p. 51).

text:
Akbar built his planned capital, Fatehpur Sikri, around the tomb/dargah of which Sufi saint, whose blessing he credited for the birth of his son, later Emperor Jahangir?
a) Shaikh Salim Chishti
b) Nizamuddin Auliya
c) Moinuddin Chishti
d) Baba Farid
sol:
**Correct Option: (a)**

**Justification:**
**Option (a): Correct.** The dargah of Shaikh Salim Chishti was built at Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's capital, and symbolised the bond between the Chishtis and the Mughal state (NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch 6, p. 160). Satish Chandra calls Shaikh Salim Chishti the patron saint of the Mughals (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 129) and records that the buildings at Sikri were begun in 1568–69, when the Kachhawaha princess was expecting Salim (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 238).
**Option (b): Incorrect.** Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya's hospice (c. fourteenth century) stood on the banks of the Yamuna in Ghiyaspur, on the outskirts of the city of Delhi (NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch 6, p. 154).
**Option (c): Incorrect.** The dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti is at Ajmer (NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch 6, p. 154). Akbar visited it fourteen times (p. 156), but his new capital was built at Sikri.
**Option (d): Incorrect.** Shaikh Fariduddin Ganj-i Shakar (Baba Farid) is associated with Ajodhan, now in Pakistan (NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch 6, p. 154). Salim Chishti was his direct descendant (p. 160), but the Fatehpur Sikri dargah is Salim Chishti's.
Hence the correct answer is option (a).

**Result:** Fatehpur Sikri holds the dargah of Shaikh Salim Chishti; Muinuddin's shrine is at Ajmer, Nizamuddin Auliya's at Delhi and Baba Farid's centre was Ajodhan.

**Salient Features: Akbar's city at Sikri**
Akbar laid the foundation of a new city and palace complex at Sikri, about 26 miles from Agra, while the Agra fort was being built (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 237).
- **The Ibadat Khana:** the Hall of Prayers for religious debate was built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575, around the cell of a Sufi saint, Shaikh Abdullah Niazi (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 93).
- **The Jama Masjid:** Satish Chandra calls it the most magnificent building at Sikri, with an interior courtyard of unusually large proportions (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 239).
- **The Panch Mahal:** the five-storied Panch Mahal stands in the city; at Fatehpur Sikri Akbar also set up a 'house of translation', where the Mahabharata was rendered into Persian as the Razmnama (NCERT Class 8, Exploring Society Part 1, Ch 2, p. 41).
- **Water for the palaces:** water from the lake below was lifted up to supply running water and the fountains of the palace complex (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 238).

**Exam Fact:** Outside Fatehpur Sikri Akbar built two establishments to feed the poor, Dharmapura for Hindus and Khairpura for Muslims, and later a third, Jogipura (Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II, PDF p. 97).

text:
Arrange the following Jain Tirthankaras in chronological order (earliest to latest):
1. Neminatha
2. Parshvanatha
3. Munisuvrata
4. Mahavira
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
a) 1-3-2-4
b) 3-1-2-4
c) 3-2-1-4
d) 1-2-3-4
sol:
**Correct Option: (b)**

**Justification:**
In the traditional Jain list of twenty-four Tirthankaras, the four names stand in this order:
- **Munisuvrata (3)** is the 20th Tirthankara, the earliest of the four.
- **Neminatha (1)** is the 22nd Tirthankara.
- **Parshvanatha (2)** is the 23rd Tirthankara (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, p. 83; II PUC History, Ch 4, PDF p. 44).
- **Mahavira (4)** is the 24th Tirthankara (DSERT Class 6 Social Science Part 1, 2026-27, p. 82), the last of the twenty-four (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 48).

The sequence is therefore 3-1-2-4.
**Option (a): Incorrect.** 1-3-2-4 places Neminatha, the 22nd, before Munisuvrata, the 20th.
**Option (b): Correct.** 3-1-2-4 follows the numbering: 20th, 22nd, 23rd, 24th.
**Option (c): Incorrect.** 3-2-1-4 starts correctly but places Parshvanatha, the 23rd, before Neminatha, the 22nd.
**Option (d): Incorrect.** 1-2-3-4 places Munisuvrata, the 20th, after both Neminatha and Parshvanatha.
Hence the correct answer is option (b).

**Result:** Munisuvrata (20th), Neminatha (22nd), Parshvanatha (23rd) and Mahavira (24th) give the order 3-1-2-4.

**Salient Features: Mahavira and the Tirthankara tradition**
According to Jain tradition, Mahavira was not the founder of Jainism but the last of the 24 Tirthankaras, the "makers of fords" (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 48).
- **The first Tirthankara:** Jain tradition regards Rishabha as the founder of the sect and the first Tirthankara, and the Yajur Veda mentions three Tirthankaras, Rishabha, Ajitanatha and Aristanemi (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 48).
- **Mahavira's birth:** Vardhamana was born around 540 BCE in Kundagrama, a suburb of Vaishali; his father Siddhartha was chief of the Jnatrika clan, and his mother Trishala was a Lichchavi princess, sister of the chief Chetaka (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 48).
- **Enlightenment:** he left home at 30, wandered for 12 years and, in the 13th year, at the age of 42, attained enlightenment; he then came to be called Jina or Mahavira, "the Great Conqueror" (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 48).
- **The fifth vow:** of the five Jain doctrines, only the fifth, brahmacharya (continence), is said to have been added by Mahavira, the other four being taken over from earlier teachers (R.S. Sharma, *Ancient India*, p. 62); Parshvanatha preached the four principles of ahimsa, satya, asteya and aparigraha (II PUC History, Ch 4, PDF p. 44).

**Exam Fact:** Buddhist texts refer to Vardhamana Mahavira as Nigantha Nataputta (Tamil Nadu Class 11 History, p. 48).
